events.headline: Bills' DJ Moore grabs ankle after big preseason debut catch, avoids serious injury
events.detail: Moore opened his Bills preseason debut Saturday (Aug. 15) against Carolina by hauling in three catches for 61 yards on Buffalo's first two drives, including a 33-yard connection with Josh Allen, before grabbing his right ankle/foot on the sideline after his last catch and walking off under his own power. He gave Allen a thumbs-up on the way out, and early reporting indicates the injury is not considered serious, though it ended his day with most of the starting offense already out of the game.
events.so_what: The on-field connection with Allen is the clean signal this format cares about for a locked-in WR1 price in Buffalo's offense; the ankle scare reads as precautionary given he walked off and gave a thumbs-up, but confirm he's back to full practice before this league's 2026-08-23 draft since any lingering ankle issue would cut into a route-running-dependent receiver's value.

events.headline: Jaguars' first depth chart lists Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. as RB co-starters
events.detail: Jacksonville's first unofficial depth chart of camp lists 2025 fifth-round pick Tuten and Rodriguez separated only by an "OR" atop the running back room, with veteran Ameer Abdullah also in the mix for touches. All three are expected to see work in Friday's preseason slate as the staff sorts out the pecking order.
events.so_what: Another true committee is this format's worst RB outcome since 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back consolidating touches, not a three-way split — this caps both Tuten and Rodriguez at speculative RB4/handcuff prices rather than a clean starter valuation until preseason snap counts show real separation. Watch the next couple of preseason games before locking either into a draft-day price.

events.headline: Nabers not suited up for Giants' preseason opener, still not contact-cleared
events.detail: Nabers was not in uniform for Saturday's (Aug. 15) preseason opener against Minnesota, one game removed from the Aug. 13 milestone of catching passes on his first four non-contact team reps. He still has not been cleared for contact, making it a real question whether he manages even a cameo before Week 1. JuJu Smith-Schuster (knee) and Jalin Hyatt (ankle) also sat out, giving young receivers Malachi Fields and Dalen Cambre an extended look.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 13 item — non-contact team reps were real progress, but sitting the actual preseason opener with no contact clearance yet is a sober reset on how close he is to Week 1, not a setback exactly, just a reminder the runway is short. Hold at a modest discount to a clean WR1 price and watch for an actual contact-practice clearance as the next real trigger before this league's 2026-08-23 draft. Direct stash relevance for bwalsh89, this league's Nabers/Dart owner from 2025.

events.headline: Rams' Puka Nacua carries groin injury plus real suspension risk into Week 1
events.detail: Nacua left Tuesday's (Aug. 11) joint practice against Dallas with a groin injury the Rams call minor, and as of Thursday (Aug. 14) his practice reps remain limited with his Week 1 status not yet clear. Separately, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported this week that the NFL is actively reviewing Nacua's offseason conduct (a civil lawsuit alleges he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark at a New Year's Eve party; no criminal charges were filed) and called it "possible" he's suspended for the Rams' Week 1 game at San Francisco. The personal-conduct policy sets a six-game floor for a first violation in this category, with aggravating factors able to push it higher.
events.so_what: This is a two-front risk on a locked-in WR1 price: the groin issue is likely a short-term hold, but a live suspension threat with no resolution timeline is a real reason to shade Nacua's draft price down from a clean top-5 WR slot until the league rules, since a multi-week PPR-caliber hole to start the season is exactly the kind of downside this format's half-PPR/2-FLEX math can't shrug off. Check Sleeper/beat coverage right up to draft day (2026-08-23) for a ruling.

events.headline: MarShawn Lloyd starts and takes every first-drive snap in Packers' preseason opener as Jacobs sits with groin injury and live suspension risk
events.detail: With Jacobs out (groin, first reported Aug. 6), Lloyd started Green Bay's preseason opener Thursday (Aug. 13) and took every snap on the first drive, working on early downs, in the passing game and in pass protection. Separately, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported this week (Aug. 11-14) that Jacobs' personal-conduct-policy investigation (stemming from a May 2026 domestic-disturbance call with no charges filed) remains open with the league still weighing discipline, and a suspension is a real possibility before Week 1; the policy sets a six-game floor for a first domestic-violence violation. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Friday (Aug. 14) that Jacobs could return to practice as soon as next week, likely coming back late in the week if he does, and continues to call the groin injury not serious.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11/13 items — LaFleur's 'back next week' framing caps the groin issue itself as a short-term markdown, but the genuinely live suspension threat with no resolution timeline is still the bigger risk to Jacobs' draft price: a multi-week absence to open the season would hand Lloyd real starting-caliber volume in this format's bell-cow-friendly scoring. Worth actually rostering Lloyd as insurance given the shallow 5-man bench, and shading Jacobs down from a clean early-round RB price until the league rules, ideally before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Bucs' Emeka Egbuka diagnosed with stable toe sprain, expected to play Week 1
events.detail: Egbuka left Wednesday's (Aug. 12) practice early after getting rolled up on and limping off, an injury scare that initially looked worse than it was. Further testing led a specialist to diagnose a stable toe sprain, per the Tampa Bay Times' Rick Stroud, and the team is "very optimistic" it won't jeopardize his season-opener availability.
events.so_what: Egbuka is Tampa Bay's clear WR1 target hog in this half-PPR format after a huge rookie season; a stable-sprain diagnosis with no real timeline concern means the scare shouldn't move his price, but confirm he's back to unlimited practice reps before this league's 2026-08-23 draft just to be safe.

events.headline: Mahomes a full participant in camp roughly eight months post-ACL/LCL surgery, targeting Week 1 return
events.detail: Mahomes has been a full participant at Chiefs training camp about eight months after surgery to repair a torn ACL and LCL suffered in Week 15 of 2025. He said this week his knee "feels great" and that his real target remains the Sept. 14 regular-season opener at Denver, not Kansas City's Aug. 15 preseason opener against the Rams, which coach Andy Reid said there's a "pretty good chance" he sits out.
events.so_what: A full-participation camp with no setbacks is the clearest health signal yet on an ADP that already prices in some post-major-knee-surgery risk; in this format's 4-pt-passing-TD, low-passing-value scoring Mahomes still needs his legs back for full rushing-adjacent value, so his actual Week 1 clearance (not the meaningless preseason opener) is the checkpoint to watch before this league's 2026-08-23 draft.

events.headline: Waddle misses Broncos' preseason opener as expected; Payton expects him back at practice next week
events.detail: Waddle sat out Friday's (Aug. 14) preseason opener against Atlanta as the Aug. 12 item flagged was increasingly likely, extending an absence that dates to a leg strain first surfacing Aug. 5. Coach Sean Payton told reporters afterward he expects Waddle back on the practice field next week.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 12 item — missing the opener confirms the trend, but Payton's 'back next week' framing caps this as a short-term hold rather than a deepening concern; recheck once he's actually practicing again before shading his post-trade WR2 price further.

events.headline: Tyreek Hill still unsigned in mid-August, waiting for a contender fit and full ACL clearance
events.detail: Hill remains a free agent nearly six months after Miami released him, recovering from a torn ACL suffered early in the 2025 season. His agent says he's waiting for full medical clearance before signing and wants to land with a contender; ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports "multiple teams" have interest, with the Chiefs (his original team) the most-mentioned fit alongside Buffalo, Baltimore, the Chargers, 49ers and Patriots.
events.so_what: Completely unrostered and unschedulable for this league's 2026-08-23 draft — not worth a pick or even a late dart until he's actually signed, since he has no team, offense, or practice reps to project from yet. Worth a last check right before the draft for a landing spot, and a clear early-FAAB priority the week he does sign given the name-brand ceiling.

events.headline: Dobbins limited to individual work as Broncos beat Falcons 27-7 in preseason opener; Coleman gets extensive run
events.detail: Dobbins remained limited to individual drills for Friday's (Aug. 14) preseason opener at Atlanta and did not play, still working back from the soft-tissue issue first reported Aug. 10. With Dobbins out, rookie Jonah Coleman got an extensive workload in the 27-7 win, continuing the camp buzz around his role.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 10 item — a full missed preseason game, not just a practice absence, is a real accumulation of lost reps for Dobbins against a rookie who keeps taking advantage of every opportunity handed to him. Still hold Dobbins as the lean for Denver's early-down role, but Coleman's price now needs to reflect genuine handcuff-plus-touchdown-usurper upside rather than a pure camp-buzz speculative flier; recheck once Dobbins is back to full team drills.

events.headline: 49ers' Ricky Pearsall undergoes season-ending PCL surgery
events.detail: Pearsall announced on Instagram Thursday (Aug. 13) that he had surgery to repair the PCL in his right knee, ending his 2026 season before it started. The knee had been persistently swollen through camp after he first injured it in Week 4 of 2025; his targeted recovery window is roughly nine months, putting a return around mid-May 2027 OTAs. He's played just 20 of a possible 51 regular-season games across his first three NFL seasons.
events.so_what: San Francisco's WR2 job behind Mike Evans (Aug. 11 item) is now fully vacant before the draft, not just contested — Deebo Samuel is the likeliest full-time beneficiary of the vacated snaps in Kyle Shanahan's run-funnel offense, with Jauan Jennings the clear No. 3. In half-PPR/2-FLEX, this removes a name some boards still carried as a discount buy and nudges Samuel's price up a notch in the McCaffrey/Kittle/Evans-led target pecking order.

events.headline: Titans' Pollard-Spears split looks genuinely even in preseason opener under new OC Brian Daboll
events.detail: In Thursday's (Aug. 13) preseason opener, Pollard played 57% of snaps (50% of designed rushes, 33% route participation, 2 catches for 11 yards, 35 rush yards) against Spears' 43% of snaps (38% of rush attempts, 50% route participation, a rushing TD on 3 carries for 2 yards). The beat read: "the coaching staff has told us multiple times that they view Pollard and Spears interchangeably, which matches Week 1 of the preseason." Daboll was hired as Tennessee's OC this offseason under new HC Robert Saleh.
events.so_what: This format's top RB tier wants one back consolidating touches, not a genuine timeshare — an actual even preseason split under a new play-caller is a real markdown on Pollard's price relative to a clean lead-back valuation, and it bumps Spears from pure handcuff to a real FLEX-relevant piece if the split holds. Both currently project more as touchdown-or-bust RB3s than clean starters; recheck preseason Week 2 usage.

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love starts over Tyler Allgeier in Cardinals' preseason opener, plays 75% of snaps
events.detail: In Thursday's (Aug. 13) preseason opener, the No. 3 overall pick started at running back over Allgeier and played 16 of 22 snaps (75%) across two drives, totaling 14 touches for 58 yards (5.3 YPC). It's the first live-game confirmation of the first-team-reps trend first reported in practice on Aug. 9.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 9 item — a preseason start plus a 75% snap share is a stronger signal than practice reps alone, and this format's bell-cow premium means Love should now price as a clear low-end RB1/high-end RB2, not a speculative add. Allgeier slides further into handcuff/complementary value; James Conner's eventual workload (still not fully cleared for 11-on-11s) remains the swing factor once he returns.

events.headline: Browns name Deshaun Watson starter for preseason opener; Shedeur Sanders gets the start Aug. 22
events.detail: Coach Todd Monken confirmed this week that Watson starts Cleveland's preseason opener Saturday (Aug. 15) at Chicago, with Sanders set to start preseason Week 2 against Buffalo on Aug. 22. Monken said both will play meaningful snaps in the opener, including a two-minute drill each, and the preseason finale vs. New England (Aug. 27) will factor into the Week 1 decision.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 8 item — a structured, alternating-starts plan (not a clear front-runner emerging) confirms Cleveland's QB1 job is still genuinely open into September. This format pays no draft capital for either passer, but the battle stays the key swing factor for Njoku and the Browns' receiving corps' target stability, and it's relevant for mfkr and DiaperDutyDaddy (this league's rounds 2-4 QB-sniping threats) tracking a possible in-season Sanders takeover.

events.headline: Panthers rule Chuba Hubbard out for the rest of the preseason with hamstring strain; Brooks confirmed for bulk of first-team reps
events.detail: Hubbard felt something grab during one-on-ones Wednesday (Aug. 12) and was taken for an MRI. Coach Dave Canales called it 'a legit hamstring' injury Thursday (Aug. 13), set him week-to-week, and follow-up reporting Friday (Aug. 14) firmed that into Hubbard being held out for the remainder of the preseason entirely — though Canales said he's 'very confident' Hubbard will be ready for Week 1 and the team will 'be smart about it' rather than rush him back. With Hubbard sidelined, Brooks — who missed all of 2025 with a second torn ACL — is confirmed to take the bulk of first-team reps in Saturday's (Aug. 15) preseason opener against Buffalo.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 12 item — this is no longer a healthy Brooks earning real ones-reps alongside Hubbard, it's Hubbard sidelined for the full preseason and Brooks getting the workhorse look in his first live action since his 2024 rookie year. A real, if short-term, markdown on Hubbard's clean bell-cow price and a genuine bump for Brooks; Canales' 'confident for Week 1' framing keeps this short of a full committee call, but Saturday's snap count is now the clearest signal available before the draft.

events.headline: DeVonta Smith misses seventh straight practice, but pre-practice route work signals a return is close
events.detail: Smith sat out Thursday's (Aug. 13) practice for a seventh consecutive session with the hamstring injury first reported Aug. 4, but worked through route-running drills with trainers beforehand — a step ahead of rookie Makai Lemon, who remains in a similar limbo. The Eagles open the preseason Saturday (Aug. 15) against Baltimore.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11 item — seven missed practices is a real stretch, but the pre-practice route work is the clearest 'getting close' signal yet, and beat coverage now floats a return as soon as next week. Half-PPR target-hog scoring keeps Smith a locked-in WR1 price on the 'not serious' framing that's held throughout; recheck once he's actually back in team drills.

events.headline: Chiefs' top-four receivers practice together for first time as Worthy nears a full return; Rice already cleared for contact
events.detail: Rice, working back from an offseason knee debridement (further complicated by a 30-day jail stint for a probation violation), progressed from rejoining team drills (Aug. 11) to taking and absorbing full contact in 11-on-11s (Aug. 12) without issue and says he's '100% locked in.' Worthy, sidelined since Aug. 1 with a shoulder sprain that turned into a longer-than-expected absence, has been back in pads in limited fashion over his last several practices and could be a full participant later this week; this camp's practice this week marked the first time Mahomes' top four receivers — Rice, Worthy, Tyquan Thornton and rookie Cyrus Allen — were all on the field together.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11/12 items — Rice is now the cleaner buy of the two ahead of Kansas City's Aug. 15 preseason opener against the Rams, while Worthy's longer absence keeps him at a modest health discount in Mahomes' catch-and-run game until he's actually back to full-speed reps; recheck once Worthy logs an unlimited practice or preseason snaps.

events.headline: Vikings' first unofficial depth chart lists Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason as RB co-starters
events.detail: Minnesota's first depth chart of the preseason, released Wednesday (Aug. 12), lists Jones and Mason separated only by an "OR" at the top of the running back room. Mason started all five games Jones missed in 2025 and finished with 758 yards and 6 TDs on 159 carries to Jones' 548 yards and 2 TDs; Jones remains the clearly superior receiving option. Zavier Scott, Demond Claiborne and Jermar Jefferson round out the room.
events.so_what: A true committee is this format's worst RB outcome since 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back consolidating touches, not a timeshare — an "OR" atop the unofficial chart is a real markdown on Jones' price relative to a clean lead-back valuation, though Jones' receiving-game edge keeps him the safer bet in Kevin O'Connell's scheme. Watch joint-practice and preseason snap splits before locking either into a set draft-round price.

events.headline: Falcons confirm Tagovailoa as preseason-opener starter, but Stefanski still won't name a Week 1 QB
events.detail: Coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed Wednesday (Aug. 12) that Tagovailoa will start and play at least the first series in Friday's (Aug. 14) preseason opener against Denver, with Penix — still not fully cleared for 11-on-11s off his ACL tear — not in the mix for that game. Stefanski again said it's too early to name a regular-season starter.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 10 item: a confirmed preseason-opener nod is a real, if incremental, signal Tagovailoa is the front-runner and not just the reps leader, but Stefanski's continued hedge means this still isn't a locked designation. Doesn't move Bijan Robinson's price; the next real trigger for Atlanta's passing-game pieces is Penix's full-practice clearance.

events.headline: Croskey-Merritt stays 'firmly entrenched' as Commanders RB1 despite Rachaad White's strong joint-practice showing
events.detail: In Wednesday's (Aug. 12) joint practice with Miami, White broke a long outside-zone run showing good contact balance and continued building on the pass-catching role he's carved out this camp, but beat reporters still have Croskey-Merritt as the clear starter given his fit in Washington's new outside-zone scheme. Jeremy McNichols and rookie Kaytron Allen round out the room.
events.so_what: Half-PPR volume scoring rewards Croskey-Merritt's early-down role, but White's receiving-game separation keeps him relevant in a format where 2 FLEX can start a legitimate passing-down back — price Croskey-Merritt as the lead-back RB2/3 and White as a flex-worthy handcuff/PPR complement, not purely speculative, especially with Laremy Tunsil's blindside injury (Aug. 9 item) adding pressure to protect Jayden Daniels' checkdown game.

events.headline: McCaffrey misses a third straight 49ers practice, team still calling it 'tightness'
events.detail: McCaffrey sat out again Wednesday (Aug. 12), a third consecutive missed practice as he sits out San Francisco's joint session with Tennessee. OC Klay Kubiak called it 'tightness' and said the team is 'just managing' him; head coach Kyle Shanahan reiterated he isn't concerned.
events.so_what: Updates the Aug. 11 item — still hold at his current price as this format's clearest bell-cow RB1, but three straight missed days is now a real pattern past the original single-day 'maintenance' framing, and it's the clearest workload-trim signal yet for an age-30 back coming off a 413-touch 2025. Worth a fast recheck once he's back to a full practice.

events.headline: Giants list Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr. as co-starters on first unofficial depth chart
events.detail: New York's first depth chart of camp, released ahead of the preseason opener against Minnesota, lists Skattebo and Tracy as co-starters at running back — the only offensive position without a clear No. 1. Tracy opened 2025 as the starter but was passed on the depth chart even after returning from injury, with Skattebo nearly doubling his snap count in Weeks 4-5 before his own rookie-season-ending ankle injury; Devin Singletary rounds out the room's top three.
events.so_what: A true committee is this format's worst RB outcome — 2 FLEX and half-PPR reward one back who consolidates touches, not a 1a/1b split, so neither Skattebo nor Tracy should be priced as a clean RB2 off this alone. Track joint-practice and preseason-game snap counts as the real signal; whichever back separates first is the one worth the earlier pick.

events.headline: Vikings name Kyler Murray starting QB over J.J. McCarthy
events.detail: Coach Kevin O'Connell named Murray the Vikings' Week 1 starter on Tuesday (Aug. 11), ending a training-camp competition that began when Minnesota signed him to a one-year deal in March after Arizona released him. O'Connell cited Murray's command of the offense and decision-making in camp; McCarthy moves to backup behind him. Minnesota opens Sept. 13 against Green Bay.
events.so_what: This format pays QB almost nothing through the arm (4-pt pass TDs, 1/25 yards) but scores rushing at RB rates — Murray's history of 5-6+ carries a game with real yards-after-contact makes him exactly the rushing-QB archetype worth a rounds 3-5 pick here, now locked into a full-time job throwing to Justin Jefferson. Directly on Sladsous's radar: their draft history runs QB rounds 4-5 favoring rushers (Lamar Jackson twice, Jalen Hurts). McCarthy falls off the board entirely as a backup.

events.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel: 'I'll use all three' of Hampton, Vidal, and Mitchell 'probably every game'
events.detail: Speaking to reporters Monday (Aug. 10), McDaniel said he plans to divide the backfield among rookie Omarion Hampton, Kimani Vidal, and free-agent addition Keaton Mitchell by matchup and 'hot hand' rather than a fixed pecking order: 'Bad news, fantasy owners. Good news is I see all three of those guys producing at a very high level. Bad news is I can't tell you which games those are.' McDaniel ran a similar committee in Miami in 2023, getting both Raheem Mostert and De'Von Achane into the top-6 fantasy backs.
events.so_what: This format's 2-FLEX/half-PPR setup pays a premium for a clear bell-cow over a split backfield — a first-round rookie's own OC publicly disclaiming a set pecking order is a real markdown on Hampton's price relative to where his draft pedigree alone would put him, and it lifts Vidal and Mitchell from waiver-only to speculative bench-stash territory behind him.

events.headline: Bears' Luther Burden expected to miss the preseason with groin injury, but on track for Week 1 opener
events.detail: Burden's Saturday (Aug. 8) groin injury — suffered tangling with CB Tyrique Stevenson in red-zone one-on-ones — will keep him out through Chicago's Aug. 29 preseason finale vs. Tennessee, but coach Ben Johnson expects him back for the Sept. 13 regular-season opener at Carolina. Burden, a 2025 second-round pick coming off a 47-catch rookie year, is stepping into the WR2 role opposite Rome Odunze now that Chicago traded DJ Moore to Buffalo earlier this offseason (this report corrects the Aug. 8 item, which mistakenly still had Moore on Chicago's roster) — Johnson has compared his ceiling to Amon-Ra St. Brown's.
events.so_what: Half-PPR reception scoring and this format's normal-depth WR/FLEX math both reward Burden's expanding target share now that Moore is gone from the room entirely, not just battling him for reps — hold at his current breakout-candidate price with a short-term missed-preseason discount, and only revisit if the absence stretches past the opener.
